values: Re-time annual commitment to program delivery pace
VP Technology and Data with Cloud FinOps support
Reset Year 2 committed purchase to a ramped schedule tied to named workloads reaching production readiness.

A Year 2 commitment should step up only as governed workloads move from pilot or planned into production. We are asking Databricks to re-time the committed purchase schedule to match actual deployment gates, with no penalty for Year 1 underuse caused by program sequencing.
Databricks gives up an immediate full Year 2 run-rate lock and accepts milestone-based consumption growth.
Buyer prepays for shelfware while planned workloads remain outside production.
Re-base support fee to consumed spend and support demand
Recalculate Business Critical Support on actual consumed platform usage until production workloads materially increase.

The current support fee is anchored to committed purchase rather than observed support demand or consumed workloads. We are asking Databricks to re-base support for the next contract year, with an automatic step-up only when production usage and support volume justify it.
Databricks gives up committed-purchase-based support economics during low-consumption periods.
Include in Year 2 commercial amendment before invoice issuance.
Support spend stays disconnected from actual workload scale and support demand.
Add carry-forward provision for unused Year 1 commitment
Carry forward unused Year 1 commitment into Year 2 or convert it into onboarding, migration, training, or implementation credits.

The contract's no-carry-forward position should not convert delayed workload adoption into lost buyer value. We are asking Databricks to preserve a negotiated portion of unused Year 1 commitment as Year 2 consumption credit or equivalent adoption services.
Databricks gives up forfeiture of a portion of unused Year 1 committed purchase.
Resolve before year-end true-up and Year 2 payment authorization.
Unused commitment expires and the buyer loses leverage before the next payment cycle.
Route future commitment through AWS Marketplace private offer
Route eligible future Databricks commitment through an AWS Marketplace private offer if it can improve enterprise discount program credit or simplify cloud portfolio governance.

Because the Databricks deployment runs on AWS, future commitment should be evaluated for Marketplace private-offer routing. We are asking Databricks to support the commercial path that maximizes the buyer's cloud portfolio economics without changing governed data-platform scope.
Databricks supports alternate transaction routing and any associated private-offer economics.
Confirm before Year 2 commercial paper is drafted.
The buyer may miss cloud-portfolio credits or negotiate Databricks in isolation from AWS commitments.
Re-price the platform services discount band after Finance loads an accepted comparable for a similar multi-year consumption-platform commitment.

This is an advisory signal, not a document-proven finding. The current package shows the commitment size and confirms benchmarking is absent, so we are asking Databricks to re-open discount-band evidence once a comparable five-year volume benchmark is available.
Databricks would move from the current discount position to a benchmark-supported tier if the buyer proves comparable market terms.
Load one accepted benchmark comparable before treating this as an executive ask in the Year 2 amendment.
The buyer may negotiate only ramp timing and credits while leaving a potentially mispriced discount band untested.
Cloud FinOps and Enterprise Data Platforms
Confirm committed-discount treatment across serverless and classic compute and load a side-by-side per-SKU cost comparison before workload migration.

This is a workload-shape signal, not a priced finding. The package shows bursty pilot jobs-compute usage, but it does not include per-SKU serverless comparison evidence, so the ask is to confirm discount parity before making serverless the default operating model.
Databricks would preserve committed-discount economics across the target compute mode or provide a clear commercial bridge for the migrated workload.
Complete before the pilot workload moves from classic jobs compute into production serverless jobs.
A technically sensible compute shift could dilute the committed discount or move spend into a SKU pattern the contract does not protect.
